events.title: City of Forest Day: Meet the West Harlem Forest
events.description:
Join Riverside Park Conservancy & Natural Areas Conservancy to explore the 7.5 acres of forest currently being restored in West Harlem!

7.5 acres of natural area are being restored in West Harlem! Join practitioners from Riverside Park Conservancy and the Natural Areas Conservancy to tour the site, meet the trees, and learn why forest restoration is critical! NY Bird Alliance will also join to share how healthy forests support local and migratory birds. Open to all ages, with kids’ crafts and activities.

events.title: City of Forest Day: The Marvelous Trees of Hippo Playground
events.description:
Join Riverside Park Conservancy and Councilmember Gale Brewer’s office to learn about the trees in and around Hippo Playground.

Join staff from Riverside Park Conservancy’s Sustainability Department and Councilmember Gale Brewer’s office to learn about the trees in and around Hippo Playground. Kids will enjoy hands-on arts & craft activities, while we share info on NYC’s first Urban Forest Plan and how to get involved stewarding trees in your neighborhood!

events.title: The Little Red Lighthouse Festival
events.description:
Celebrate Manhattan’s only remaining lighthouse with the Urban Park Rangers, readings of the eponymous children’s book, live music, local organizations, and activities for all ages! Featuring performances by Moosiki Kids, Leadlights Ensemble, General Mischief Dance Theatre, and a special presentation of Jessica Ann Carp’s Little Red Lighthouse Musical.

As the Little Red Lighthouse is more than 140 years old and in need of care, it has been determined that the Lighthouse will again be only be open for a limited number of tours during this year’s Festival, led by the NYC Park Rangers! As in years past, tours will be first come, first served, with tickets distributed on site at 12pm. To safely and comfortably accommodate visitors, we have reduced the total number of visitors we can accommodate, and tours are limited to the first 200 attendees.

The Little Red Lighthouse is beloved by New Yorkers and visitors alike. Join us in our quest to ensure that the Little Red Lighthouse can safely receive visitors for years to come. Together we can keep the light shining!

Check back for more information!

events.title: Works in Public 2026 Unveiling
events.description:
The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation are proud to present Works in Public 2026, a year-long outdoor public art exhibition in Riverside Park. The exhibition features four new site-specific sculptures by League artists: Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca in Riverside Park South at 61st Street, and Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson  in Riverside Park North at 145th Street.

Schedule:

1:45pm – Meet in Riverside Park North, 145th St. to unveil the new rosk by Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson.
3:00pm – Board our free shuttle to Riverside Park South
3:45pm – Arrive at Riverside Park South, 61st St to unveil the new works by Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca.

About the Art and Artists: 

Lindsey Francis Jones, City in Shapes, City in Fish
City in Shapes, City in Fish invites viewers into the artist’s visual language through a cityscape of abstract shapes and color. Inspired by the craft and community of printmaking, the work incorporates images of six fish etched onto selected plexiglass, contributed by fellow printmakers and artists: Laurissa Widrick, Felix Bladbjerg, Kait Waldman, Stan Overstreet, Barbara Ganmen, and Scarlett Patino.

Clare Burson, Unearthed.
UNEARTHED is an installation of three steel forms inspired by the ancient Plain of Jars in Laos. It asks us to consider the inevitable and unexpected ways that history imposes itself on the present. When experienced with its accompanying soundscape, UNEARTHED also reminds us that our shared public spaces are nexus points for an infinite number of narratives that connect individuals and communities across time, those who lived here before us and those who will come after us.

Alicia Ehni, Balancing 
A Peruvian shaman once told Ehni to carry a lemon in her purse, that it brings great harmony in life and in interactions with others. Two fractured pre-Columbian ceramics carry ancient coastal knowledge, opening possibilities to imagine a different future. Balancing reflects on the fragile relationships between people, nature, and the built environment.

Robert Franca, The Chairs
The Chairs explores family as the foundation through which we understand ourselves and the world. Seen through a child’s perspective, the chairs embody imagination, openness, and freedom from conventional rules. Their human-like forms suggest movement and the ability to change. Ultimately, the chairs speak to the importance of finding balance — within ourselves, within families, and in navigating the challenges and uncertainties of an ever-changing world.

events.title: It’s My Park Day: Fall Edition!
events.description:
It’s My Park Day is a biannual event where we come together to celebrate and take care of our beloved ParkTender gardens. Our ParkTenders steward various landscaped areas throughout the Park, some with one season of stewardship under their belts and some with decades of dedication to their gardens.

During the fall edition of It’s My Park Day, our ParkTenders and field staff work together with volunteers to take care of fall planting needs.
